description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

Germany faced the tank threat during World War I and tried ranged anti-tank ammo first with reversed bullets. The transcript explains how a 7.92x57 Mauser round was modified with the slug twisted off and reinserted backward for a blunt nose, aiming to penetrate armor at close ranges (with possible spall inside tanks), but it was noted as not a great solution and could damage the rifle or injure the shooter. It then shifts to the 7.92x57 K bullet, an armor-piercing design with a tool-steel core—more effective at about 100 yards and described as having about a one in three chance to penetrate 12–13 mm armor, though it was less effective against the thicker Mark IV that entered in 1917. What other WWI anti-tank weapon ideas should we cover next?

title: Reversed & K Bullets: WWI’s Tank-Killers?
